column1: Preheat the oven to 425°F (218°C) and line one large or two small baking sheets with parchment.
In a large bowl combine the warm water, sugar and maple syrup. Add the yeast and let it sit 5 minutes until slightly foamy.
Stir in the egg, oil, salt and flour until a dough forms.
Turn the dough onto a lightly floured surface and knead about 12 minutes, adding up to 1/2 cup extra flour until smooth and no longer sticky.
Cover the dough with an upturned bowl and rest 10 minutes.
Divide into 12 pieces. Roll each into an 8–10 inch (20–25 cm) rope, loop into a ring overlapping the ends by 1–2 inches, and roll or pinch the seam to seal.
Let the shaped bagels rest 10 minutes. Meanwhile put the seeds in a bowl and bring the water with brown sugar or honey to a boil, then reduce to a simmer.
Simmer the bagels 3–4 at a time for 45 seconds per side, then drain briefly on paper towels.
While still damp, press each bagel into the seeds on all sides and arrange in a single layer on the prepared pan.
Bake 8 minutes, flip, then bake another 6–8 minutes until lightly golden. Cool on a rack.
